_notes: Manager ranking recipe. Editable: `weight` and `enabled`. Everything else is documentation copied from services/managers/ranking.py, which stays authoritative — changing `invert` or `directional` here does nothing, because those are facts about the metric rather than preferences.
Only metrics with directional=true are scored. The rest are fingerprints: they are percentiled and drawn on the page as a profile, with no good or bad end, so their weight is ignored and left at 0.
score = sum(weight_i / sum(weights) * percentile_i) over the enabled directional metrics, percentiled WITHIN THE LEAGUE, then shrunk toward 50 by matches/(matches+8).
A metric that is null for a spell scores a neutral 50 and is never punished for being missing.

`enabled` means PUBLISHED: an enabled metric is written to the payload with its raw value and its league percentile, and — if it is directional and carries a weight — counted in the score. Turning one off removes it from the page as well as from the total.

metrics.label: Set-piece balance
metrics.help: Set-piece xG created minus set-piece xG conceded, per match — the dead-ball edge at both ends, which is the part of a match a coach most directly drills.

metrics.label: Sendings off
metrics.help: Reds and second yellows per match, inverted. Real cost, but rare — roughly one per seven matches league-wide — so a single one is thin evidence rather than a verdict.

metrics.label: Protects a lead
metrics.help: Opponent xG per minute spent ahead, inverted — how much he lets the other side have once his own are in front.

metrics.label: Chases a game
metrics.help: His side's own xG per minute spent behind — whether going a goal down produces chances or only urgency.

metrics.label: Half-time correction
metrics.help: Second-half xG difference minus first-half xG difference — what changes once he has had fifteen minutes with them.

metrics.label: Substitution impact
metrics.help: xG difference per minute in the fifteen minutes after his first change minus the fifteen before it, with the scoreline held constant so a chasing side is not credited for chasing.

metrics.label: Self-inflicted
metrics.help: Errors leading to a shot or a goal, per match, inverted. Opta flags about one a match across both sides, so this is a low-volume number that moves a lot between seasons — weighted lightly on purpose.

metrics.label: Card rate
metrics.help: Cards per 100 opponent passes, inverted — fouling expressed per chance to foul, so a side that presses and therefore sees less of the ball is not punished for it.

metrics.label: Press height
metrics.help: How far upfield his side's tackles, interceptions, challenges, recoveries and fouls happen. It is where actions occurred, not where the team stood.

metrics.label: PPDA
metrics.help: Opponent passes allowed per defensive action in the opponent's 60% of the pitch. Lower is a tighter press — but a press is a choice, not a virtue, so it is not scored.

metrics.label: Time to win it back
metrics.help: Mean seconds between losing the ball and having it again. Measured from possession runs — a run is consecutive events by one side — so it is the real out-of-possession spell, not a proxy like PPDA. Spells longer than 60s are dropped: past that it is a stoppage, a restart or a goal celebration rather than football. NOT SCORED, and deliberately so — a fast regain is a high press, a slow one is a low block OR a side being outplayed, and this number cannot tell those last two apart.

metrics.label: Won back within 5s
metrics.help: Share of losses won back inside five seconds — the counterpress. Cleaner than the mean above, because five seconds is short enough that it can only be a deliberate immediate press and not the slow decay of a low block. Read the two together: a side can be quick here and still slow on average, which is a press that either works at once or drops off.

metrics.label: Pass length
metrics.help: The median length of his side's passes, in pitch units — the everyday distance they play at, not the long ones.

metrics.label: Directness
metrics.help: Share of passes that move the ball more than 15 units upfield. High is vertical football, low is patient — neither is better.

metrics.label: Territory
metrics.help: Share of his side's touches taken in the final third — where the team lives when it has the ball.

metrics.label: Fast breaks
metrics.help: Share of his side's shots that arrive on the counter rather than from settled possession.

metrics.label: Minutes concentration
metrics.help: How tightly minutes are held by a few players. High is a settled eleven, low is a rotated squad.

metrics.label: Players used
metrics.help: How many players took at least 25% of the minutes available across the spell — the size of the group he actually trusts, not the number who got on the pitch. Minutes concentration says the same thing as an index; this says it as a number of men, which is the version anyone can read.

metrics.label: XI churn
metrics.help: Average number of changes to the starting eleven from one match to the next. Injuries and congestion move this as much as preference does.

metrics.label: First substitution
metrics.help: The minute he typically makes his first change — an early hook and a patient bench are both real methods.

metrics.label: Substitution intent
metrics.help: Share of changes that bring on a different position from the man going off: changing the shape rather than swapping like for like.

metrics.label: Shape repertoire
metrics.help: How many different starting formations he has picked. A longer spell has had more chances to vary, so read it beside the match count.

metrics.label: Shape changes
metrics.help: Formation changes made inside a match, per match — how often he re-draws the side while it is playing.

metrics.label: Short corners
metrics.help: Share of corners played short instead of delivered into the box — a dead-ball preference, not a dead-ball skill.

metrics.label: Foul height
metrics.help: How far upfield his side's defensive fouls are committed. It tracks press height almost mechanically, so read the two together.
